docs.title: Decide on a check item (valid, invalid, to do)
docs.summary: For each check, select the words in your translation, then mark the item valid or invalid, or leave it to do.
docs.where: Inside a checking tool › Your translation and the buttons ✓ Mark valid, Invalid, To do
docs.text: Every check item ends with a decision: Button Meaning --- --- ✓ Mark valid The translation is right for this item. Invalid Something needs fixing. To do Not decided yet (the default). For each item in Translation Notes and Translation Words. Read the highlighted quote. Tap the word(s) in Your translation that render it: "Tap the word(s) in your translation that render the highlighted quote." Tap again to unselect. Click ✓ Mark valid or Invalid. Click To do to undo a decision. Marking an item does not move you on. Click the → arrow at the top right of the item (above the quote) to go to the next item. The ← arrow goes back one item. You can also click any item in the rail. To fix the text, click ← Back to translating. See Edit a verse after checking. The decision is saved at once. The item counter ("Item n of N") and the arrows sit at the top of the item. If you have scrolled down, scroll up to see them. Known issue: Your translation shows your words without punctuation, and a word with an apostrophe can look split (for example "God's" shows as "God s"). Your text in Translate is not affected. Use the Invalid filter later to find everything you still need to fix. If the resource version changed since the book was checked, a check may not save: "This check was not saved. The project's resource changed since this book was checked — update the resource first, then check again. Nothing was lost." Tapped words are highlighted in Your translation. After ✓ Mark valid the item shows as valid in the rail and the count "{decided} of {total} resolved" goes up. The header shows "Item n of N".

docs.title: Bookmark a check
docs.summary: Flag a check item to come back to it later, for example to discuss with your team.
docs.where: Inside a checking tool › ⚑ Bookmark
docs.text: A bookmark marks a check so you can find it again. It does not change the decision. When you are unsure and want to come back, or want to raise an item at a team meeting. In a checking tool, open the item. Click ⚑ Bookmark. It now reads Bookmarked. Later, choose the Bookmarked filter in the rail to see all bookmarked items. To remove it, click Bookmarked again. Combine with a comment to say why you bookmarked it. None known. The button changes from Bookmark to Bookmarked. The rail shows Pablo under PAUL with an orange flag and 1:1. The Bookmarked filter lists only bookmarked items.

docs.title: Write a check comment
docs.summary: Add a note to a check item about what you decided or what to ask your team.
docs.where: Inside a checking tool › ✎ Add a comment
docs.text: A check comment is a short note attached to one check item. To record the reason for a decision, or a question for a consultant. In a checking tool, click Add a comment. The box is titled My comment on this check. Its hint is "Say what you decided, or what to ask your team about this check." While it is open, the button changes to Hide comment. Done and Delete comment are in the box. Hide comment closed the box. The button went back to Add a comment, and the Commented count stayed at 0. Check comments can be deleted. User comments in Understand cannot. See Write a user comment. None known. A box titled My comment on this check opens with the hint "Say what you decided, or what to ask your team about this check." While the box is open the button says Hide comment.

docs.title: Filter and sort check items
docs.summary: Narrow the list to what still needs work, and change the order of items.
docs.where: Inside a checking tool › the rail › filter chips and Sort
docs.text: The rail on the left of a checking tool lists the items. You can filter and sort it. Filter Shows --- --- All every item To do undecided items Invalid items marked invalid Bookmarked items with ⚑ Commented items with ✎ Sort buttons Tool --- --- By word / By verse Translation Words (Bible) By verse / By category Translation Notes (Bible) By word / By frame Translation Words (stories) By frame / By category Translation Notes (stories) Open a checking tool. Click a filter chip in the rail. Next to Sort, click one of the two buttons to change the order. Click an item to open it. Finish a pass with To do, then fix problems with Invalid. When nothing matches, the rail says "Nothing matches this filter." The item that was already open can stay in the main pane. None known. The filter chips read All · 223, To do · 223, Invalid · 0, Bookmarked · 0, Commented · 0. Invalid is filled. Under the filters, Sort is followed by two buttons; the selected one is filled. If nothing matches, the rail says "Nothing matches this filter."

docs.title: Community Checking preview
docs.summary: Read the whole book as a printed page, set up the page, and export a copy for reviewers.
docs.where: Check › Community Checking card › Open →
docs.text: Community Checking shows your book the way it will look when printed, so it can be read aloud or shared with the community for feedback. When you want to read the book as a whole, or make a copy for reviewers. Click Check, then Open → on the Community Checking card. If the last checking tool you used opens instead of the list, click ← All checking tools. Scroll the preview. In Page setup, choose: Columns: 1 or 2 Spacing: Single or Double Paper size: A4 or Letter Drop-cap chapters and Verse numbers: on or off Use Export to make a file. See Export a PDF, Export USFM and Export a Scripture Burrito. Note: Spacing and Paper size arrived in 4.0 rc.1 (Increment 8, PRs 387 and 380; issues 142 and 381). The exported PDF uses them: with Letter selected, the PDF page is US Letter (8.5 × 11 in). Spacing Double is useful when reviewers want room to write between the lines of a printout. Changing the page setup only changes the preview and the export. It does not change your project, so the save indicator stays on Saved. The card on the picker says "Next · read {chapter} aloud" to suggest a reading plan. On Sample English the preview title is Titus. Verse 1 prints "Paul, a servant of God." The comma and the period are here, unlike the Translation Words and Translation Notes panes, which show "Paul a servant of God". Verses 2 through 16 each say "[ verse not yet drafted ]". Chapter 1 is shown because it has a drafted verse. Columns is 1, Spacing is Single, Paper size is A4. Drop-cap chapters and Verse numbers are on. Footnotes is off and cannot be switched on. Export was not opened, and the setup was not changed. Footnotes is shown but cannot be switched on yet. Page setup is not remembered after you leave the screen, and each book starts on Columns 1, Single, A4. Set it again before you export. With nothing drafted, the page shows the book title and "Nothing is drafted in this book yet." It does not show a Preview eyebrow or per-verse placeholders. Page setup: Columns 1 or 2, Spacing Single or Double, Paper size A4 or Letter, Drop-cap chapters on, Verse numbers on, Footnotes off. Double doubles the line spacing in the preview, Single brings it back. Letter makes the page wider. Changing the page setup does not change the project: the save indicator stays on Saved. The note says Incomplete draft. Undrafted verses and chapters show as not yet drafted. Undrafted chapters before the first drafted chapter or after the last are left out.

docs.title: Open the Align tool
docs.summary: Align links each word of your translation to the original-language word it translates. Open it from the Check screen.
docs.where: Check › Align card
docs.text: Alignment connects your words to the Greek or Hebrew words they translate. The other checks use these links to highlight your words, and aligned exports (such as USFM, aligned) carry them. After drafting a chapter or book, usually before or during checking. Click Check. If the last checking tool you used opens instead of the list, click ← All checking tools. Click the Align card (it says "Link your words to the original language…"). Pick a verse in the rail on the left. Link the words (see Link words). Click ← All checking tools to go back. The To do filter lists verses still to align, including undrafted ones. Clicking the verse you are already on keeps your word bank as it is (new since alpha.7, PR 416). On Sample English, Titus has one drafted verse. The progress line says "0 of 1 verses aligned". The filters still count the whole book: All · 46, To do · 46, Invalid · 0. Verse 1:1 shows the draft. Verses 1:2 on say Not drafted yet. Verse 1:1 already has "Paul" under the Paul card, so the bank says "1 of 5 words placed". The verse still counts as not aligned. ← Back to translating at the bottom of the rail returns to Translate. ← All checking tools returns to the tool list. Align is for Bible books only. Open Bible Stories have no Align card. A verse that does not match exactly one source verse in the project's numbering cannot be aligned: "This verse has no single source verse". With nothing drafted, the screen says "Nothing to align yet". The rail on the left shows ← All checking tools, the heading Align, the book name, a progress bar and "{done} of {total} verses aligned". Filter chips with counts: All, To do, Invalid. Undrafted verses show Not drafted yet. The main area shows the verse reference, the source word cards and the Word bank · your translation.

docs.title: Link your words to the source
docs.summary: Click a word in the word bank and then the card it belongs under, or drag it there.
docs.where: Align › Word bank · your translation and the word cards
docs.text: Each source word has a card . Your verse's words sit in the word bank . Placing a word under a card links them. In Align, open a verse. Click a word in the Word bank · your translation. Click the card it belongs under. Or drag the word onto the card. Repeat until every word is placed. To undo a link, click the placed word ("Click to un-align"). It goes back to the bank. When you are done, click ✓ Mark valid (see Mark an alignment done). Open How alignment works for a short reminder on the screen. You can mark a verse done even if some words stay unplaced (for example words your language adds). Known issue: After you click a word in the bank, no hint tells you what to do next. Just click the card the word belongs under. If you change the verse in Translate after aligning, the changed words go back to the word bank. Place them again and mark the verse valid again. See Editing a verse you already checked or aligned. The word you click is highlighted in the word bank. The placed word appears under the card and leaves the bank; the count "{placed} of {total} words placed" goes up. When the bank is empty it says "Every word is placed. Click a placed word to send it back."

docs.title: Align a phrase (merge and split cards)
docs.summary: When several source words are translated together, merge their cards into one phrase card. SPLIT undoes it.
docs.where: Align › drag one word card onto another › SPLIT
docs.text: Sometimes two or more source words become one word in your language, or a phrase translates a phrase. Merge the cards so the words can be linked together. In Align, drag a word card onto the card next to it ("Drag onto another word card to merge them into a phrase"). The two cards become one phrase card. Place your word(s) under the phrase card. To undo, click SPLIT. Merge only neighbouring words that belong together. Known issue: If you already placed words under a phrase card, SPLIT leaves all of them under the first card (for example both "Jesus" and "Christ" stay under Jesus, and the Christ card is empty). Click a misplaced word to send it back to the bank, then place it under the right card. See the known issue under Tips. The merged card holds both source words and shows SPLIT. SPLIT ("Split back into single words") restores the separate cards.

docs.title: Align to the gateway text or the original language
docs.summary: Align to the gateway words you can read (which already carry the link to the original), or directly to the Greek or Hebrew words.
docs.where: Align › the switch Gateway · ULT / Original · Greek (or Original · Hebrew)
docs.text: tC4 can align in two ways: Gateway · ULT : "Align to the gateway text you can read — its words already carry the original-language alignment." Easier if you do not read Greek or Hebrew. Original · Greek or Original · Hebrew : "Align directly to the original-language words." The source heading reads "Original language · Greek", and the cards are Greek only. A word already placed in gateway mode stays in its slot. On Titus 1:1, Paul stayed under Παῦλος. Either way, the saved links point to the original language. In Align, open a verse. Click Gateway · ULT or Original · Greek (Hebrew for Old Testament books). Link the words as usual. The hint under the switch tells you which mode is active. Gateway mode needs aligned gateway text for the verse. If missing: "The gateway lens needs the gateway source text with alignment data for this verse." In Gateway · ULT mode the cards show gateway words, with the original-language words beneath each ("Original-language words this gateway word is aligned to"). In Original · Greek mode the cards show Greek words.

docs.title: Alignment suggestions
docs.summary: tC4 can learn from the verses you have already aligned and suggest links for the next ones. You confirm or reject each one.
docs.where: Align › Suggestions › Suggest links
docs.text: Suggestions propose links based on how you aligned earlier verses in the same testament. Nothing is saved as aligned until you confirm it. After you have aligned several verses by hand. In Align, tick Suggest links in the Suggestions row. The row says "Drawn from N verses you have already aligned". (A "Learning from your aligned verses…" message may show first, but usually it is too quick to see.) Open a verse and click Suggest. Check each dashed chip. Click its ✓ to confirm it. Or click Accept all or Reject all. Reset clears the suggestions. Align a few verses carefully by hand first. Suggestions are only as good as what they learn from. The switch is remembered for each project on this computer. Known issue: Suggestions are often wrong in this build, especially after only a few hand-aligned verses. Words can land under cards in the order they come rather than by meaning. Check every chip before you confirm it. Do not use Accept all without checking: ✓ Mark valid will then accept the wrong links too. You must confirm or reject suggestions before marking the verse done (see Mark an alignment done). If nothing fits, it says "Nothing to suggest for the words still in the bank." With the switch off the row says "Off. Turn on to get links proposed from the verses you have already aligned." With too little data it says "No aligned verses yet in this testament — align a verse by hand first." or "Too few aligned verses to learn from yet — align a few more by hand." After Suggest, suggested words appear on their cards as dashed chips with ✓.

docs.title: Mark an alignment done
docs.summary: When a verse is aligned, mark it valid. It counts toward the verses-aligned progress.
docs.where: Align › ✓ Mark valid
docs.text: ✓ Mark valid says "This verse's alignment is done, even if some words stay unplaced. Any later change takes it back." Finish linking the words of a verse. Confirm or reject any suggestions. Click ✓ Mark valid. Marking valid does not move you to the next verse. Click the next verse in the rail, or the → arrow at the top right. If you edit the verse later, the valid mark is taken back and the verse needs another look. Upgrading the original-language text marks existing alignments invalid, so they must be reviewed (see Upgrade scripture texts). The verse turns valid in the rail and "{done} of {total} verses aligned" increases. If suggestions are still open, the app refuses with "Confirm or reject the suggested links first."

docs.title: Start an Open Bible Stories project
docs.summary: Create a project for translating all fifty Open Bible Stories into your language.
docs.where: Home › + Add a project › New Open Bible Stories
docs.text: Open Bible Stories (OBS) is a set of 50 short Bible stories, each told in numbered frames with a picture. A stories project in tC4 holds your translation of all 50. When your team translates OBS, for example as a first project before Scripture. On Home, click + Add a project. In the Add a project dialog, click the second card, New Open Bible Stories. The New Open Bible Stories dialog opens in its place. Type a Project name (for example "Help Demo Stories"). Type the Language name and its Code. Choose the Text direction. Leave the Checking language on English unless you have another complete OBS set. Keep the Script font on "Noto Sans (default)", or pick another. Click Create stories →. On Home, click a story tile on the new card to open it. With no remembered place, the story opened in Understand. After you have used Translate, opening it again returns there. Keyboard: in the Add a project dialog, press Tab until the New Open Bible Stories card has a blue ring, then press Enter or Space. Esc closes the dialog. The New Open Bible Stories dialog has no back button. To choose another kind of project, click Cancel, then + Add a project again. It opens on the three cards. "English ships with the app and has the complete OBS set, so it is preselected." Known issue: Your first click in the dialog can scroll it and take the cursor out of the field, so the first letters you type are lost. Click the field again and check what you typed. The dialog says everything can be changed later. The name and language still cannot. Text direction, script font, and Checking language can be changed afterwards in Project settings. The project does not open by itself after you create it. Open a story from its card. Creating OBS projects on Windows had a reported problem (issue 402, open). The dialog New Open Bible Stories says "All fifty stories, in your language. Everything here can be changed later." Fields: Project name, Language name, Code, Text direction (Left to right / Right to left), Checking language (English preselected, with a RECOMMENDED badge) and Script font (starting on Noto Sans (default)). After Create stories → you are back on Home. The new card shows the OBS badge and "50 stories" with three story tiles.

docs.title: Find a story on Home
docs.summary: The stories card shows your three most recent stories. Show all 50 to pick any story.
docs.where: Home › the stories project card › story tiles › Show all {n} stories
docs.text: Each story is a tile, like a book tile for a Bible project. A tile shows the story number and title, the percent drafted, and when you last edited it. On Home, find your stories card (it has the OBS badge). Click a tile to open that story. To see every story, click "Show all 50 stories →". To collapse, click "Show recent stories only →". Continue where you left off with Resume reopens the last story and frame you edited. None known. The collapsed card shows three tiles (recently edited stories, or stories 1–3 for a new project). Clicking "Show all 50 stories →" lists every story with its percent drafted. "Show recent stories only →" collapses it again.

docs.title: Translate a story
docs.summary: Draft the story title, each frame, and the reference line, one at a time, with the picture and the gateway story beside you.
docs.where: Open a story › Translate
docs.text: The story Translate screen is like Bible drafting, but the units are the title, the frames and the reference. To draft or edit a story. Open a story from Home (or pick one in the Stories rail; Toggle story list shows or hides it). Click Draft the title and type the story title. Click Save, or just click outside the box, to save. For each frame, click "Draft frame N", read the picture and gateway text, and type your translation. Click Draft the reference and translate the reference line (for example "A Bible story from: Genesis 1-2"). To change a saved part, click it (Edit this text). The frame numbers in the rail show which frames are drafted. Use the helps panel (Toggle helps panel) for notes and word links while drafting. With no frame open for editing, the Stories rail still listed plain names ("Story 1", "Story 2", and so on) and did not show percentages. Frame 2 was highlighted in the rail while the page was scrolled to frame 16. Known issue: While a frame is open for editing, the rail has shown the same plain names. A story's percent drafted may not update right away. Known issue: With no comments on the story, the Comments tab says "Nothing in this chapter." (Bible wording). It means the story has no comments yet (see screenshot 4). Note: Verse spans and verse numbers do not exist in stories. They are only for Bible books. If the gateway story is missing, the screen says "Gateway text is unavailable." with Get source. If no picture matches, the screen lists the image lines it could not find. The rail lists Stories. The main area shows Story title, each "Frame N" with its picture and Gateway story text, and Reference. Empty parts show buttons: Draft the title, "Draft frame N" and Draft the reference. While editing: a box with the hint Type your translation…, and Save / Cancel. The source badge reads like "Gateway story · v9 · pinned".

docs.title: Understand a story
docs.summary: Read each frame with its picture and the story helps, and write a comment for each frame.
docs.where: Open a story › Understand
docs.text: The same idea as Read a passage before you translate, for stories. Comments are written per frame. Open a story and click Understand. Read the title and each frame with its picture. Click a frame to see its notes, word links and questions in the helps panel. Until you click a frame, the panel may show the helps for another frame. Click in the frame's comment box, type your comment, then click outside to save. The comment box under the story title reads "What does this frame say, and what will be hard to render?" Nothing was typed in it. In the helps panel, story notes are labelled like verses. On frame 1 each card said NOTE v1. The first note quoted "the beginning", then "created", "the universe", and "the earth". The notes were in English. Known issue: Your first click in a comment box selects the frame and can scroll the page, and only part of what you type may be saved. Click the box again once the page stops moving, type, and check that the whole comment was kept. If a comment fails to save, the app says "The user comment was not saved — edit the box and leave it again to retry." There is no simplified-text tab for stories. Saved comments cannot be emptied, as for Bible projects. The screen says "Read the story and its helps before you translate." Each frame shows its picture, the gateway story text and a comment box. The helps panel has Notes, Words and Questions for the selected frame.

docs.title: Check a story
docs.summary: Check a story with Translation Notes and Translation Words, frame by frame.
docs.where: Open a story › Check
docs.text: Checking a story works like checking a Bible book (see Check). The unit is the open story, and items point at frames. Open a story and click Check. If the last checking tool you used opens instead of the list, click ← All checking tools. Pick Translation Words or Translation Notes. Next to Sort in the rail, click By frame to go through the story in order. Tap the words in your translation and decide: ✓ Mark valid, Invalid or To do. Use bookmarks, comments and filters as usual. The tool list for stories uses Bible wording, such as "One focused pass through the whole book". For stories it means the open story. A story uses its own resources: the story notes (en obs-tn) and the story word list (en obs-twl). Switching to a Bible project and back does not mix them up (fixed in Increment 8, issue 434). Item 1:0 is the story title. Frames are 1:1, 1:2 and so on. An undrafted frame says "This frame is not drafted yet. Draft it first, then return to check." There is no alignment for stories. The picker shows three cards, in this order: Translation Words, Translation Notes and Community Checking. There is no Align card. Each card shows a progress count, not a "ready" label. Items are labelled story:frame (the item header reads like "Story 1 1:1" for story 1, frame 1). The source pane is Gateway · story text. The rail's Sort buttons for Translation Words are By word and By frame.

docs.title: Story preview and export
docs.summary: Preview a story as a page with its pictures, adjust page setup, and export PDF, Story Markdown or a Scripture Burrito.
docs.where: Open a story › Check › Community Checking › Open →
docs.text: The story version of Community Checking. You preview the story as a page, set pictures and layout, then export a copy for reviewers. Open a story and click Check. If the last checking tool you used opens instead of the list, click ← All checking tools. Click Open → on the Community Checking card. Optional: turn Pictures on or off, and choose Pictures above or Pictures wrapped. Click Export and pick Export PDF, Story Markdown (.zip) or Scripture Burrito (.zip). See Export stories as PDF or Markdown and Export a project as a Scripture Burrito. There is no Align card on stories — only Translation Notes, Translation Words and Community Checking. Pictures wrapped puts a small picture beside each frame's text, so more of the story fits on a page. Pictures above puts a large picture above each frame. Stories have no Spacing or Paper size choice. The story PDF on this build was A4. A run of undrafted frames is one line, without a picture. The on-screen note begins "Incomplete draft. The export shows each run of undrafted frames or stories as one line, without pictures…" The story PDF is always A4; there is no Letter choice for stories yet. The first page of the story PDF has only the story title. The frames start on page 2. The preview is labelled PREVIEW and Story 1. Frame 1 shows its picture and "God made everything." A line reads "[ frames 2–16 not yet drafted ]". A reference line was not in view. Page setup Layout is Pictures above or Pictures wrapped. Pictures can be on or off. A story's Page setup has no Columns, Spacing or Paper size rows. Those are for Bible books only. The Export menu offers Export PDF, Story Markdown (.zip) and Scripture Burrito (.zip).

docs.title: Export stories as PDF or Markdown
docs.summary: Save a print-ready PDF of the stories, a Story Markdown zip, or both alongside Scripture Burrito — from the same Export menu as Bible.
docs.where: Open a story › Check › Community Checking › Open → › Export
docs.text: From Community Checking on an Open Bible Stories project, Export offers three ways to take the stories out of the project: a dated PDF, a Story Markdown zip of the fifty story files, and a Scripture Burrito zip of the whole project. PDF — a printable reading copy for reviewers, with or without pictures. Story Markdown — the story Markdown files for other OBS tools. Scripture Burrito — a full project zip to import elsewhere (see Export a project as a Scripture Burrito). Open a story and click Check. If the last checking tool opens instead of the list, click ← All checking tools. On Community Checking, click Open →. Optional: set Page setup (Pictures, Layout). Click Export, then the format you want. A save window opens with a suggested file name. Keep it or type another, then save. When the file is saved, the panel shows "Saved <file name ". Close it with its ✕. Undrafted frames are not each given a picture. Incomplete draft. says the export shows each run of undrafted frames or stories as one line, without pictures. For story 1 with frames 1–2 drafted, the PDF had both pictures and one line "[ frames 3–16 not yet drafted ]". To save a second PDF with another layout (for example Pictures wrapped), change the layout, export again, and type a new name in the save window, such as Sample Stories-wrapped.pdf. If nothing is drafted, draft at least one frame (or the title) before exporting a PDF. On Linux, the save window is the system file window. Its title bar shows a long "blob:http://127.0.0.1…" address; that is normal. It opens in your Downloads folder, with the suggested name selected in the Name field. On this build its Save and Cancel buttons were above the visible part of the window: press Enter to save, or Esc to cancel. Cancel the save window: no success toast. A failed PDF shows a red Report and leaves the project unchanged. The story PDF is A4 only, and its first page has only the title; the frames start on page 2. Export PDF with Pictures on worked on this packaged Linux build. An older build failed with "Printing failed"; if you see "The app could not print the PDF with its pictures…", turn Pictures off and export again. The PDF needs the desktop app (not offered in a plain browser). The Export menu lists Export PDF, Story Markdown (.zip) and Scripture Burrito (.zip). Story Markdown (.zip) shows Saved Sample Stories-stories-2026-10-05.zip; Export PDF shows Saved Sample Stories-2026-10-05.pdf; Scripture Burrito (.zip) shows Saved Sample Stories-2026-10-05.zip. The message appears only after the file is saved. Cancel shows no message.

docs.title: Download source texts
docs.summary: Download source texts and helps for another gateway language from Door43.
docs.where: Inside a project: Project settings › Manage source texts → › Get source texts
docs.text: A gateway language is the language your team reads the source in. English is included. Other gateway languages can be downloaded from git.door43.org. When your team wants to read and check in a gateway language other than English, or a resource is missing. Open the project, open Project settings, then click Manage source texts →. Home no longer has a Source texts button. If the dialog says the app is offline, click Go online (see Working offline). Under Choose your gateway language, pick a language and organisation. Wait for "Reading the catalogue from git.door43.org…". Choose a Book. Check the Package contents. Selected cards are highlighted. Click a card to leave it out, or click it again to add it back. Click ⇣ Download package. Progress shows "Downloading {repo}…". When you see "✓ {book} · {language} is ready", click Close (or the round × at the top right). Each language row names the organisation and the published notes, words, and academy versions. On Sample English the English row was "unfoldingWord · notes v89 · words v89 · academy v89". Español (Latinoamérica) was es-419 gl, notes v66, words v37, academy v4. Two rows are both named Français: Xenizo (notes v2.0) and MVHS (notes v0.0.2). Neither was opened. To use the downloaded language for checking, open Project settings and choose it under Checking language. See Change the checking language. A separate Use for checking step was not how the language was chosen. The versions shown next to each language in the list (for example "notes v89 · words v89 · academy v89" for English) are the latest releases published on Door43. They are not the versions your project uses. A checking tool shows the version it uses under its filters, for example "en tn · v86". Needs internet. Pinned resources, on this open, was a heading with Check for updates. The pinned list itself was not shown. Two gateway rows can share one language name. Both French rows say Français. The organisation name under the title is what tells them apart. Opening English on Sample English says "This project already checks against English." The book is Titus. Change language is at the top. The package cards are Translation Academy (en ta), Translation Questions (en tq), Translation Notes (en tn), and Translation Words + Links (en tw). Four source-text cards are marked Always included: en t4t ("Source files for Translation For Translators."), en ult ("unfoldingWord Literal Text (formerly ULB)"), en ust ("unfoldingWord Simplified Text (formerly UDB)"), and the Greek New Testament (el-x-koine ugnt). Close and Download package are both at the bottom. The "already checks" line does not hide Download package. Nothing was downloaded. Some organisations publish nothing tC4 can use for a book: "This organisation publishes nothing tC4 can use for {book} in {lang}." If some downloads fail, the dialog lists them: "Some resources did not install — …" The dialog Get source texts says "A literal and a simplified text with notes, words, and questions — aligned to the original." After picking a language: Book, Package contents as a list of cards (selected cards are highlighted; Always included cards cannot be left out) and ⇣ Download package. When done: "✓ {book} · {language} is ready".

docs.title: Change the checking language
docs.summary: Choose which installed gateway language this project checks against. The choice is in Project settings. Decisions that match a check in the new notes carry over; the rest come back as work.
docs.where: Home › project card › Settings › Project settings › Checking language
docs.text: Checks are made against the helps of one gateway language (the checking language ). You choose it in Project settings, from the languages whose notes are on this computer. When your team moves from English helps to helps in a language they read better. Download the notes for the new language first if that language is not listed (see Download source texts). On Home, click Settings on the card, then Manage source texts →. Under Choose your gateway language , pick the language, for example Español (Latinoamérica) (es-419 gl), and click ⇣ Download package . When it is done it says "✓ Titus · Spanish (Latin American) is ready". On Home, click Settings on the project card. Checking language is in that dialog. It is not in the top bar. Read the sentence under the heading, for example "This project checks in English · unfoldingWord." Each downloaded language has its own row, for example Español (Latinoamérica), es-419 gl, Spanish (Latin American). Click the other language. A dialog opens: "Change checking language to Spanish (Latin American)?" It says how many of your decisions were made against the notes you are leaving, for example "3 decisions in Titus were made against the notes you are leaving.", and for each tool how many carry over: "Titus · Translation Notes: 0 carried over, 3 to check again". Click "Change to Spanish (Latin American)" to confirm, or "Keep en" to stay with the current language. Project settings now says "This project checks in Spanish (Latin American) · es-419 gl." and the Spanish row is marked Current. Open Check › Translation Notes. The package line reads git.door43.org/es-419 gl/es-419 tn · v66 · primary gateway language, and the quotes are Spanish, for example "conforme a la fe". The progress line counts the decisions that carried over (with 0 carried over: "0 of 112 resolved"). Decide the checks again. ✓ Mark valid saves, the indicator shows Saved, and the count goes up (1 of 112, then 2 of 112). After a full restart, Resume opens Check on the Spanish notes, in the same tool. Which decisions carry over. A decision carries over only when the new notes have a matching check: the same note on the same words of the original text. Notes in another language are often written differently: the Spanish notes for Titus 1:1 split one English note into several shorter ones, and two of the English notes have no Spanish note at all. So three English decisions can have nothing to match, and the dialog then says "0 carried over, 3 to check again". That is correct, not a fault. Decisions that do not carry over are not deleted. They stop counting, and those checks come back as work. A book that was finished will not be finished any more. The new language's checks start as To do, including words you had marked Invalid in English, because they are new checks. The Current badge is the language the project checks in now. Known issue: The same language has two names. The lists say "Español (Latinoamérica)"; the sentence under Checking language, the change dialog and the download message say "Spanish (Latin American)". The button to cancel the change names the language code instead: "Keep en". Known issue: If you change to another language and then back again, a check you had marked Invalid yourself comes back as To do, not Invalid. Mark it again. The set must be complete: "Download the {lang} notes, words and academy before pinning them — a language set must be complete." The change is refused if books already checked are not covered by the new language. Checking language lists the installed languages. The current one is marked Current. The sentence under the heading is "This project checks in {lang} · {org}." Choosing the other language opens "Change checking language to {lang}?" with how many decisions in each book were made against the notes you are leaving, and for each tool how many carry over and how many to check again (for example "Titus · Translation Notes: 0 carried over, 3 to check again"). After the change, Check counts exactly the decisions the dialog said would carry over, shows the new notes' quotes, and every check can be decided again with Saved showing.

docs.title: Update pinned helps
docs.summary: See which resource versions your project uses, and move to newer releases when you are ready.
docs.where: Home › project card › Settings › Manage source texts → › Pinned resources › Check for updates
docs.text: A project pins exact versions of its helps so checks stay stable. Updating is always your choice. When you want the latest notes and word articles, for example at the start of a new book. On Home, click Settings on the project card. Project settings opens. (It is no longer in the top bar — issue 505.) Click Manage source texts →. The project opens, with Get source texts on top. If the dialog says the app is offline, click Go online. In Pinned resources, click Check for updates. If "Use the internet?" appears, click Continue . The button reads "Asking git.door43.org…", then each set shows ✓ Up to date or "Upgrade N resource(s)" with each move, for example en tn v86 → v91 · 2026-09-26. If a set has updates, click "Upgrade N resource(s)". Read the confirmation. If nothing is checked yet, it says "Nothing you have already checked will be affected." Click Upgrade, or Keep the current release. "Decisions that match a check in the new release carry over. The rest stop applying, so those checks come back as work… Nothing is deleted." Known issue: Pinned resources does not list the versions your project uses until you check for updates, so offline you cannot see them there. The versions next to each language in the list below are the latest published releases, not your project's (for example "notes v89" while the project uses en tn v86). To see the version a tool uses, look under the filters in that tool, for example "en tn · v86". For a project that checks against English, the primary set and the fallback set are both English (Primary set · en, Fallback set · en), so the same upgrades are listed twice. A project that checks in another language has that language as the primary set and English as the fallback. "Equipo Ejemplo — Tito y Jonás" showed Primary set · es-419 ✓ Up to date and Fallback set · en "Upgrade 4 resource(s)". A new project made with build 79d3017 starts on the English v91 helps that come with the app, so both sets say ✓ Up to date. Projects imported from older work keep the versions they used (for example en tn v86), and Check for updates offers the newer ones. Nothing changes until you click Upgrade. Needs internet: "The app is offline. Go online to check for updates." tC4 does not check for updates automatically. Pinned resources shows a Check for updates button. When the app is offline it says “The app is offline. Go online to check for updates.” and the button is disabled. After Check for updates each set (the primary set, and any fallback set) shows ✓ Up to date or an "Upgrade N resource(s)" button. The confirmation "Upgrade the {set}?" lists each move and says how many decisions are affected, with Keep the current release and Upgrade.

docs.title: Update scripture texts
docs.summary: Move the project to a newer release of the Greek or Hebrew text, or of the gateway Bible.
docs.where: Home › project card › Settings › Manage source texts → › Pinned resources › Check for updates › Scripture texts
labels: ✓ Every scripture text is up to date
docs.text: New since alpha.7. Besides the helps, you can update the scripture texts the project is pinned to. On Home, click Settings on the project card, then Manage source texts →. The project opens, with Get source texts on top. Go online if needed, then in Pinned resources click Check for updates (click Continue if "Use the internet?" appears). Look under Scripture texts. Each text with a newer release has its own row, for example Gateway Bible en ult v89 → v91 · 2026-09-26. If everything is current, it says ✓ Every scripture text is up to date. Click Upgrade on a row. Read the confirmation and confirm. Upgrading the gateway Bible changes nothing in your work: "No alignment and no check decision will change. The source pane will show the new text." Upgrading the original-language text keeps every alignment, but marks the affected ones invalid so you check them again. Which original-language text is offered: only the one your books need. A project with only New Testament books (for example Titus) is never offered the Hebrew text (hbo uhb), even if it pins an old one. A project with an Old Testament book gets the Hebrew row when its pin is older: "Equipo Ejemplo — Tito y Jonás" (Jonah and Titus, pinned hbo uhb v2.1.30) showed Original-language text hbo uhb v2.1.30 → v3.0.0 · 2026-08-14. A new project made with build 79d3017 already uses the texts that come with the app (for example en ult and en ust v91), so it says ✓ Every scripture text is up to date. Needs internet. A text with no newer release gets no row. In these tests no Greek (el-x-koine ugnt) row appeared. Save any open alignment edit first: "an alignment edit is not saved. Save it, then try again." Scripture texts lists the Original-language text and the Gateway Bible. If all are current: ✓ Every scripture text is up to date. Otherwise each row has Upgrade. Upgrading the original text warns "The alignments of {n} verse(s) will be marked invalid." An Original-language text row appears only for a text that one of the project's books needs (Hebrew for an Old Testament book, Greek for a New Testament book), and only when the project pins an older release.

docs.title: Fix a missing resource
docs.summary: When a checking tool needs a resource that is not on this computer, tC4 offers three ways to get it.
docs.where: Check › a tool card › Fix this…
docs.text: A project pins exact resource versions. If a pinned version is missing (for example a project copied from another computer), the tool card shows a problem and Fix this…. When a checking card says Needs downloading or Unavailable offline. In Check, click Fix this… on the tool card. Choose one option: 1 · Download the pinned version (needs internet): click ⇣ Download it. The file is checked against the pinned version before it is installed. If the app is offline, the button is greyed out; click Go online first. 2 · Use a version that is installed : click one of the installed versions listed (each card shows its version and "installed"). A confirmation shows how many decisions carry over or are kept as invalid; click Re-pin to accept. 3 · Sideload it from a file : drop a Scripture Burrito zip of that exact release, or browse for it. To leave without changing anything, close the dialog with the round × at the top right or the Close button at the bottom. Offline, only options 2 and 3 work. The dialog says "The app is offline, so it cannot download. Go online, re-pin to an installed version, or sideload a file." An imported translationCore 3 project often pins older releases (for example en tn v87) than the ones installed with the app, so its cards can show Unavailable offline until you go online or re-pin. Hard to see in a new project, because the bundled resources are already pinned. You see it with projects imported or copied from another computer. The dialog title reads "{tool} needs a resource that is not on this computer". Three options: "1 · Download the pinned version", "2 · Use a version that is installed" (Re-pin), "3 · Sideload it from a file". The dialog closes with the round × at the top right or the Close button at the bottom.

docs.title: Working offline
docs.summary: tC4 works without internet. It only goes online when you ask it to, for downloads and updates.
docs.where: Everywhere. Internet is used only when you choose Go online.
docs.text: Everything you need to translate and check English-gateway projects is installed with the app, and your projects are stored on your computer. The app starts with internet access switched off in the app. It goes online only when you click Go online. Needs internet Works offline --- --- Download source texts Create, open and resume projects Update pinned helps Translate, Understand, Check, Align Update scripture texts Community Checking and export Option 1 in Fix a missing resource Import Work normally. No internet is needed. When you need a download, open Source texts and click Go online. A tool that needs a missing resource says Unavailable offline but never blocks the rest of your work. After you restart tC4 it is offline again. Click Go online when you need the network, for example to download or check for updates. Offline: Keep regular backups of the projects folder (see Where your projects are stored); there is no online sync yet. Sharing to Door43 and team sync are not built yet. When the app is offline, Source texts shows "The app is offline, so it cannot read the Door43 catalogue." and Go online. Drafting, checking, aligning, exporting and importing all work offline.

docs.title: Project settings
docs.summary: Open a project's settings from the Settings button on its Home card. Change the text direction, the script font, or the checking language, or manage its source texts. The name and language are shown but cannot be changed yet.
docs.where: Home › project card › Settings › Project settings
docs.text: Each project has settings for how its text is written and shown, and for which gateway language it checks against. Open them from the project's card on Home: click Settings on the right of the card. There is no settings button in the top bar: to change a setting while you work, go back to Home (click the project name at the top left), then click Settings on the card. The dialog's title is Project settings, with the project name and its number of books under it (for example "Sample Titus · 1 books"). Setting Can change? --- --- Bible name Not yet Language name, Code Not yet Text direction (Left to right / Right to left) Yes Checking language Yes. Choose an installed language in this dialog. Change the Text direction or the Script font if you need to, then click Save changes. Under Checking language, choose a language or click Manage source texts →. Choosing another language is covered in Change the checking language. To close without saving, click the round ✕ at the top right or press Esc. What changed in Increment 8: the Project settings button used to be in the top bar inside a project. It moved to the Settings button on each Home card (issue 505). A new Bible such as Sample Titus (Español, es) checks in English: "This project checks in English · unfoldingWord.", with English marked Current. On Sample Titus the subtitle read "Sample Titus · 1 books". On Sample Stories it read "Sample Stories · 0 books". The stories dialog still labels the name field Bible name. Before Spanish notes were installed, the only checking-language row was English, with unfoldingWord under it, and the sentence "This project checks in English · unfoldingWord." Sample Import says "Sample Import · 1 books". The language name is blank, the code is es, and the sentence is "This project has no checking language yet. Choose one below." English and Español (Latinoamérica) are both listed, and neither is marked Current. Nothing was chosen. Sample Stories had no Spanish row. The sentence was "This project checks in English · unfoldingWord." That matches the English notes on story 1. Sample English, an English Bible, says the same sentence: "This project checks in English · unfoldingWord." The English row is marked Current. The subtitle is "Sample English · 1 books". Language name English and code en are greyed out. Nothing was saved. After translation notes were downloaded, a second row appeared: Español (Latinoamérica), es-419 gl, Spanish (Latin American), marked Current. The sentence was "This project checks in Spanish (Latin American) · es-419 gl." Pick the font that shows your script's letters correctly. The list on Sample Titus was Noto Sans (default), Charis SIL, Scheherazade New — Arabic script, Awami Nastaliq — Nastaliq, and Padauk — Myanmar. docs.title: Messages that protect your project
docs.summary: When tC4 finds something unexpected, it stops rather than risk your work, and tells you what to do. Damaged import files are refused with a reason and a code, and nothing is created.
docs.where: Shown as a warning when you open, save, import or export
docs.text: tC4 checks your project files before it writes, and checks files you import before it creates anything. If something does not match, it refuses and explains. It never imports only part of a damaged file. When you open, save or export Message starts with What it means What to do --- --- --- "A file changed outside the app." Another program changed a project file. Open the project again; tC4 fixes changed book files or names the ones it cannot fix. "A story file was changed outside the app." A story file was edited outside tC4. Undo the outside change, then open the project again. "This computer's change folder holds another computer's changes." A project folder was copied by hand. Ask for help. Use export and import to move projects. "… has no drafted verse yet, so the PDF has nothing to print. Draft at least one verse of this book, then export the PDF again." Nothing to print in this book. Draft at least one verse, then export again. "The app could not print the PDF…" The PDF could not be made. The project did not change. Close the app, open it again, and export again. For stories, try with Pictures off. "The app stopped to protect your project. This is a problem in the app." An internal check failed. Ask for help. When you import A damaged file shows a red box on the review step, This file cannot be imported , with the reason and a code. The code line ends "Nothing will be created from this file. tC4 does not import only the correct parts of a damaged file." The subtitle says "Fix the file and choose it again." Code Example reason What to do --- --- --- import.damaged.usfm-parse "no-id.sfm has no \id line, so the book is not known." Also: a file that is not UTF-8 text, two files for the same book, or a marker with no end marker. Fix the USFM file in a text editor (for example, add \id TIT as the first line), then choose it again. import.damaged.truncated "damaged-truncated-burrito.zip is not a complete zip file." The zip was cut off (for example, an unfinished download or copy). Export or copy it again. import.damaged.no-manifest "… has no manifest.json, so it is not a translationCore 3 project." Choose the zip that translationCore 3 (tC3) exported. import.damaged.corrupt-entry "… is damaged: the file … in it does not match its checksum, so it cannot be read." Export the project from translationCore 3 again. import.name-exists "A project with this name is already on this computer. Change the Bible name, then import again." Type another Bible name on the review. import.write-failed "The partly written Bible was removed, so nothing was added to this computer. Your files are unchanged." Try again. If it happens again, ask for help. Read the message. It always says whether your work is saved, or that nothing was created. Follow its advice. For a damaged import file, click ← Choose other files to pick a good file, or Cancel to stop. If it says "Ask for help", contact your support person and keep the project folder as it is. Most of these messages say "Your work is saved", "Nothing was overwritten" or "Nothing will be created from this file." The code (for example import.damaged.truncated) helps your support person. Write it down or take a screenshot when you ask for help. After a refused import, Home has no new card and no new project folder. Known issue: Under a red "This file cannot be imported" box, the Checks column can still show a green Details row ("Language and name were read from the file…") and "Every verse is present.", with BOOKS 0. Trust the red box: the file cannot be imported. Known issue: On one run the round ✕ of the import dialog did not respond after a refused burrito. Press Esc to close the dialog. Their wording comes from the app. A damaged import file shows a red box "This file cannot be imported", the reason, and a code line that starts with import.damaged. The subtitle reads "Fix the file and choose it again." Import as a new Bible stays greyed. Only ← Choose other files and Cancel lead on. No project card and no project folder is created. A book with nothing drafted is refused for PDF with "… has no drafted verse yet, so the PDF has nothing to print. Draft at least one verse of this book, then export the PDF again."

docs.title: If the app closed unexpectedly or the window went blank
docs.summary: tC4 keeps a log of each project operation and finishes or cleans up an interrupted step at the next start. If a screen cannot be drawn, tC4 shows a message with Back to Home, and Window › Reload brings the app back without quitting.
docs.where: Automatic, the next time you start tC4. In the desktop app: the Window menu › Reload (Ctrl+R).
docs.text: New since alpha.7. Each step that changes your projects (create, import, save, upgrade…) is written to an operations log (ops log). If tC4 stops in the middle of a step, it recovers at the next start. For example, a half-finished import is removed so that no broken project is left. Since 4.0.0-rc.1 there are two more ways back: An error screen instead of a white window. If a screen cannot be drawn, tC4 shows "This screen could not be shown." with the error text and a Back to Home button. The top bar stays, so you can also go Home from there. Window › Reload. The desktop app's Window menu has Reload (Ctrl+R) and Force Reload (Ctrl+Shift+R). They reload the app inside the same window, without quitting. If the window goes white or stops responding: Open the Window menu at the top of the app window and click Reload (or press Ctrl+R). tC4 comes back on Home. Check that your projects are there, then open the project again. If you see "This screen could not be shown.", click Back to Home , then open the project again. If tC4 closed unexpectedly: Start tC4 again. Check that your projects are on Home. If an import was interrupted, import the file again. In the 79d3017 test, Window › Reload went back to Home and every project was still there. An older build sometimes turned the window white when you opened a translationCore 3 project straight after importing it. Toggle Developer Tools in the same menu is for developers; you do not need it. Developers can open an inspector with Alt+Shift+I in development builds only. The inspector is not available in the normal packaged app. The Window menu is in the desktop app only. The desktop app's Window menu has Reload (Ctrl+R), Force Reload (Ctrl+Shift+R) and Toggle Developer Tools . Window › Reload reloads the app without quitting. It comes back on Home, and every project is still there. If a screen cannot be drawn, tC4 shows "This screen could not be shown." with the error text and a Back to Home button, and the top bar stays. It does not leave a white window.
